title: Jesus: The Life
bigIdea: Jesus does not just give life. He IS Life — and He lives in you.
definition: LIFE is God's own life — found IN HIM, living IN ME, flowing THROUGH ME.

definitionPoints.body: Life is not a thing Jesus carries; it is who He is (John 1:4; 14:6).
Whoever has the Son has this life now, not one day (1 John 5:12).
Life in you must come out of you, in words and in ways (John 7:38).

distinction: Breath keeps you existing. Jesus makes you living.

arc.image: Ezekiel 47: water flowing from God's house, rising from ankles to knees to loins to a river you must swim in. "Every thing shall live whither the river cometh" (47:9).
arc.summary: I found the Life, I took His words, I walked His way, I met the Person — and now life flows out of me to everyone around me.

outcomes.byNov30: Can quote five life verses from memory and replaces one "kill word" a day with a life word
Has one habit buried and one new daily walk with Jesus started
Has spoken Scripture aloud over a "dry bones" situation — a family need, a friend, Nigeria
Has a named person they are carrying life to through December

johnNote: "I am the life" is in John 14:6 ("I am the way, the truth, and the life") and John 11:25 ("I am the resurrection, and the life"). John 8 has the closely related John 8:12: "I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life." John 8:12 pairs with John 1:4 ("the life was the light of men") and carries Episode 17. John 14:6 and 11:25 carry the summit of the month.
rhyme:
In Him was life, in Him was light,

I've got the life 'cause I've got the Son!

I declare it day and night.
Everywhere I go, the river flows,
And everything lives where the river goes!

commission.intro: Each listener names one person they will carry life to through December — someone lonely, struggling, or who doesn't know Jesus. Three commitments, on three fingers like Day 1:

commitments.body: one life-word to them every week
one act of kindness they can see

days.title: Breath or Life?

scripture.text: And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.

days.hook: A plastic plant and a real plant side by side. The presenter waters both, then pulls a leaf off each. One tears; one just bends back. "Both are green. Only one is alive."
days.story: Breath keeps you existing. Jesus makes you living.

points.head: Existing is not the same as living.
points.body: The New Testament has two words for life. Bios is the life a doctor can measure: heartbeat, breath, height. Zoe is God's own life, the kind that never runs out, and John uses zoe every time he speaks of Jesus. You can have a strong heartbeat and still be empty inside. That is existing. Jesus came to give the second kind.

points.head: Life is not something Jesus carries. It is who He is.
points.body: A delivery man brings a parcel and leaves. Jesus does not hand you life and walk away; He says, "I am the life" (John 14:6). So receiving life is never about getting a thing. It is about getting Him.

points.head: Have the Son, have life.
points.body: John makes it as simple as a light switch: have the Son, have life; no Son, no life. There is no third option. This whole month is about the one Person who is Life, and making sure every listener has Him.

days.challenge: Teach the three-finger definition to one adult tonight.
days.centralTruth: Existing is not the same as living.
days.codeLine: Breath keeps you existing. Jesus makes you living.
days.declaration: I have the Son, so I have life.

quiz.q: Which Greek word does John use every time he speaks of Jesus' life?
According to 1 John 5:12, who has life?

options: Life is something Jesus carries to you

days.title: In the Beginning Was Life

scripture.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made. In him was life; and the life was the light of men.

days.hook: A single mango seed in the presenter's palm. "Every mango this tree will ever grow is already inside this seed. Before the world began, everything life would ever be was already inside Jesus."
days.story: Before anything was, Life already was — in Him.

points.head: Before anything existed, Life already was.
points.body: Before the sun, the sea or the first tree, "in the beginning was the Word." Jesus did not begin in Bethlehem; He was already there before the beginning. Life is older than the universe, because Life is a Person who has always been.

points.head: Everything that lives was made by Him.
points.body: "All things were made by him." Every mango tree, every bird, every child in Nigeria came from His hands. The One who designed life is the One who knows how to mend it, so when something in your life is broken, go to the Maker.

points.head: His life is the light of men.
points.body: John ties life and light together. When Jesus' life enters a person, they begin to see clearly: who God is, who they are, what is right. People without His life are not foolish; they are in the dark. Life switches on the light.

days.challenge: Find three living things today and thank Jesus for making each one.
days.centralTruth: Before anything existed, Life already was.
days.codeLine: Before anything was, Life already was — in Him.
days.declaration: The One who made life lives in me.

quiz.q: According to John 1:1, what was in the beginning?
According to John 1:4, what was the life?
According to John 1:3, who made all things?

mirrors.ot: Genesis 1:1–3

days.title: Life in Himself

scripture.text: For as the Father hath life in himself; so hath he given to the Son to have life in himself.

days.hook: A phone on 2% battery, then the wall socket. "The phone needs the socket. The socket does not need the phone."
days.story: We borrow life. Jesus IS the Source.

points.head: We borrow breath; He has life in Himself.
points.body: Every breath you take is given by God, moment by moment (Acts 17:25). But the Son has life in Himself, just as the Father does. We are lamps; He is the power station. A lamp only shines while it is plugged in.

points.head: Nobody could take His life.
points.body: Jesus said, "No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself" (John 10:18). Soldiers, nails and a cross did not overpower Him. He chose to give His life for us. That is love, not defeat.

points.head: That is why death could not hold Him.
points.body: Peter said it "was not possible that he should be holden of it" (Acts 2:24). The grave can hold borrowed life, but not the Source. And because you are joined to Him, death does not get the final word over you either.

days.challenge: Notice everything you plugged in today. Ask: what am I plugged into?
days.centralTruth: We borrow breath; He has life in Himself.
days.codeLine: We borrow life. Jesus IS the Source.
days.declaration: My life is connected to the Source that never runs out.

quiz.q: What does the lesson say we do with life?
options: We borrow life; Jesus is the Source

quiz.q: According to John 5:26, what does the Son have?
According to John 10:18, who laid Jesus' life down?
options: He laid it down of Himself

mirrors.ot: Exodus 3:2–14 (the bush that burned and was not used up, “I AM”)

days.title: The Life Was the Light

scripture.text: In him was life; and the life was the light of men. And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.

days.hook: A completely dark studio. Silence. One torch clicks on. "I didn't fight the darkness. I didn't shout at it. I just switched on the light."
days.story: Where Life walks in, darkness walks out.

points.head: Where life comes, light comes.
points.body: When Jesus walked into Zacchaeus' house, Zacchaeus suddenly saw his own greed and gave half his goods to the poor (Luke 19:8). Jesus' life does not just make you feel good; it shows you the truth.

points.head: Darkness cannot overcome the light.
points.body: "The darkness comprehended it not" means it could not grasp it or put it out. Darkness has no power of its own; it is only the absence of light. There is no darkness in your home, your school or your country strong enough to put out the light of Jesus.

points.head: You beat darkness by switching on the light.
points.body: You don't fight a dark room with a broom. A child carrying Jesus' life doesn't need to shout at what is wrong: kindness, truth and prayer switch on the light. Jesus told His followers, "Ye are the light of the world" (Matthew 5:14).

days.challenge: Do one kind thing in a place that feels dark: a sad friend, a quarrel at home.
days.centralTruth: Where life comes, light comes.
days.codeLine: Where Life walks in, darkness walks out.
days.declaration: His life in me is light around me.

options: Zacchaeus left his home to follow the crowd

quiz.q: What could the darkness not do to the light?
options: Grasp it or put it out

quiz.q: How does a child carrying Jesus' life beat darkness?
options: By fighting it with a broom

days.title: Life You Can Touch

scripture.text: That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, and our hands have handled, of the Word of life; (For the life was manifested, and we have seen it, and bear witness, and shew unto you that eternal life, which was with the Father, and was manifested unto us;)

days.hook: A child reads a note from Daddy: "I love you." Then Daddy walks in and hugs them. "The note was good. The hug was better."
days.story: God didn't send a message about life. He sent Life.

points.head: God didn't send a message about life. He sent Life.
points.body: For centuries the prophets carried God's words. Then "the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us" (John 1:14). God came in a body you could see. Life became a Person you could walk beside.

points.head: People heard, saw and touched Life.
points.body: John says "our hands have handled" Him. Jesus touched lepers nobody would touch, took children in His arms and blessed them (Mark 10:16), and let a sick woman touch His garment. Life in Jesus was close, warm and reachable.

points.head: Now people should see His life in us.
points.body: Paul says the life of Jesus should be "made manifest in our body" (2 Corinthians 4:10). You may be the only Bible some of your friends ever read. When your hands help and your words heal, people touch Life through you.

days.challenge: Let your hands give life: help someone without being asked.
days.centralTruth: God came in a body you could see.
days.codeLine: God didn't send a message about life. He sent Life.
days.declaration: Someone will meet Jesus through me today.

days.title: Words That Are Spirit and Life

scripture.text: It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.

days.hook: Two sealed jars on the table, identical. One label says LIFE, the other POISON. “From the outside, they look the same. What matters is what's inside. Words are jars.”
days.story: Words are containers. His carry life.

points.head: Words are containers.
points.body: A word carries whatever is inside the speaker. When an angry person speaks, anger comes out; when a loving parent speaks, love comes out. Words are never empty.

points.head: Jesus' words carry what He is.
points.body: “It is the spirit that quickeneth” — that makes alive. Because life is in Jesus, life is in what He says. When He said, “Lazarus, come forth,” that word carried enough life to raise the dead.

points.head: Reading His Word is eating, not homework.
points.body: In this same chapter Jesus calls Himself bread. You don't eat once a month and expect to stay strong; you eat every day. A few verses read slowly each day feed the life inside you.

days.challenge: Read John 6 slowly this week, a few verses a night.
days.centralTruth: Because life is in Jesus, life is in what He says.
days.codeLine: Words are containers. His carry life.

days.title: To Whom Shall We Go?

scripture.text: From that time many of his disciples went back, and walked no more with him. Then said Jesus unto the twelve, Will ye also go away? Then Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life.

days.hook: A room of children. One by one they get up and walk out. One child stays seated. The presenter kneels beside them: “Why are you staying?” Child: “Where else would I go?”
days.story: There is no second source of life.

points.head: Many walked away when it got hard.
points.body: After a hard teaching, “many of his disciples went back, and walked no more with him.” Following Jesus is not always popular or easy, and some people leave when it stops being exciting.

points.head: Peter stayed because of whose words they were.
points.body: Peter didn't say, “I understand everything.” He said, “Thou hast the words of eternal life.” He stayed for the Person, not because every question was answered.

points.head: There is no second source.
points.body: “To whom shall we go?” Money, friends, fame and phones — none of them has the words of eternal life. When you don't understand, stay close and keep listening. Understanding comes to those who stay.

days.title: Hear and Live

scripture.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life. Verily, verily, I say unto you, The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God: and they that hear shall live.

days.hook: A noisy room — music, chatter, a blender. The presenter says one child's name quietly. The child turns. “In all that noise, you heard your name.”
days.story: Hear Him — and live.

points.head: Hearing is the door life comes through.
points.body: “He that heareth my word, and believeth… hath everlasting life.” Life does not enter because you are clever or good enough. It enters through your ears and your faith.

points.head: The dead shall hear — and live.
points.body: Jesus says even the dead will hear His voice, and those who hear will live. That is how powerful His voice is: it reaches places nothing else can reach.

points.head: What you hear every day decides what grows in you.
points.body: Whatever you listen to most — songs, videos, people — shapes you. Plant His Word in your ears every day, and life grows in you.

days.challenge: Swap 15 minutes of one screen habit for listening to the Gospel of John.
days.centralTruth: What you hear every day decides what grows in you.
days.codeLine: Hear Him — and live.

days.title: Only Speak the Word

scripture.text: The nobleman saith unto him, Sir, come down ere my child die. Jesus saith unto him, Go thy way; thy son liveth. And the man believed the word that Jesus had spoken unto him, and he went his way. So the father knew that it was at the same hour, in the which Jesus said unto him, Thy son liveth: and himself believed, and his whole house. The centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed.

days.hook: The presenter stands across the room and turns the TV on with a remote. “I didn't touch it. I didn't walk over. I just sent the word.”
days.story: His word works where His hands aren't.

points.head: His word works at a distance.
points.body: The nobleman begged Jesus to come to Capernaum. Jesus didn't travel; He spoke. Distance is no problem for His word — a sick relative in another city is still within its reach.

points.head: Believe before you see.
points.body: “The man believed the word… and he went his way.” He walked home with nothing but a promise. Faith is taking Jesus at His word before the evidence arrives.

points.head: The word was “Thy son liveth” — and at that very hour, he did.
points.body: When the servants met him on the road, the fever had left “at the same hour” Jesus spoke. The word and the result arrived together, and his whole household believed.

days.challenge: Pick one promise and say it every morning until Saturday.
days.centralTruth: His word works at a distance.
days.codeLine: His word works where His hands aren't.

days.title: Death and Life Are in Your Tongue

scripture.text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof. Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers.

days.hook: A child squeezes a whole tube of toothpaste onto a plate, then is asked to put it back. They can't. “Words are like that. Once they're out, they're out.”
days.story: Your tongue is a tap. Choose what flows.

points.head: Your mouth is a tap.
points.body: Whatever is in the tank comes out of the tap. If the tank is full of anger, anger flows; if it is full of His Word, life flows. Jesus said, “Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh” (Matthew 12:34).

points.head: Kill-words and life-words.
points.body: “You're useless.” “You'll never change.” Kill-words wound people for years. Life-words — “You can do it,” “God is with you,” “I'm sorry” — build them up. Paul says speak only what will “minister grace unto the hearers.”

points.head: Speaking life is not pretending.
points.body: It is not saying “there is no problem.” It is saying what God says about the problem. Speaking life is agreeing with God out loud.

days.challenge: Catch one kill-word today and replace it out loud.
days.centralTruth: Whatever is in the tank comes out of the tap.
days.codeLine: Your tongue is a tap. Choose what flows.

days.title: The Way, the Truth and the Life

scripture.text: Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me. … Thomas saith unto him, Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way? Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.

days.hook: A blindfolded child is handed a paper map — they're stuck. Then the presenter takes their hand and walks them across the room. "The map gave you directions. I gave you me."

points.head: Jesus doesn't give directions — He is the direction.
points.body: Thomas asked, "How can we know the way?" Jesus didn't hand him a map; He said, "I am the way." The way to God is not a list of instructions. It is a Person, and if you have Jesus, you are already on it.

points.head: The Way, the Truth and the Life come together.
points.body: You cannot take His life and refuse His way, or claim His truth and ignore His life, because all three are one Person. Many people want the blessing without the direction. Jesus offers Himself whole.

points.head: Following Him means staying close.
points.body: Following Jesus is not keeping a rulebook from a distance. It is walking beside Someone, talking with Him, and doing what He says because you trust Him. That is why the chapter opens with "Let not your heart be troubled": the way is safe when He is the way.

mirrors.ot: Isaiah 30:21 ("This is the way, walk ye in it")

days.centralTruth: The way to God is not a list of instructions. It is a Person.
days.codeLine: Jesus doesn't give directions — He is the direction.

days.title: The Narrow Gate Leads to Life

scripture.text: Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.

days.hook: A crowd of children squeezes through a wide doorway, laughing. One child turns sideways and slips through a narrow gap in the set. Behind the narrow gap: an open, green space. "Most people went that way. Only one found this."

points.head: Popular is not the same as alive.
points.body: "Wide is the gate… and many there be which go in thereat." A crowd is not proof of the right road. Many choose what is easy and what everyone is doing, and Jesus warns that road ends in destruction.

points.head: Narrow at the gate, wide inside.
points.body: The gate is narrow: you go through it with Jesus and leave some things behind. But inside, He promises you will "go in and out, and find pasture" (John 10:9). A narrow gate opens onto abundant life.

points.head: Few find it — be one of the few, and bring others.
points.body: Choosing Jesus may sometimes mean standing alone in your class or your group of friends. But the few who find the way become guides for the many.

days.title: Life More Abundantly

scripture.text: The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly. I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep. … My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand.

days.hook: A "thief" snatches a child's single orange and runs off. The "shepherd" walks in with a basket overflowing with oranges and fills the child's arms. "One came to take. One came to give."

points.head: The thief takes; the Shepherd gives.
points.body: The thief comes "to steal, and to kill, and to destroy": he steals joy, kills hope and destroys families. Jesus came for the opposite reason — "that they might have life." Learn to tell which one is at work in any situation.

points.head: Abundant means overflowing.
points.body: Abundant life is not having the most money or the newest phone. It is a life so full of God's peace, joy and love that it spills onto everyone around you. The Good Shepherd gave His own life to make it possible.

points.head: Abundance belongs to sheep who stay near the Shepherd's voice.
points.body: "My sheep hear my voice… and they follow me." The sheep the thief catches are the ones that wander off. Stay close, and "neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand."

mirrors.ot: Psalm 23

days.declaration: I have life, and more than enough to share.
days.centralTruth: The thief comes to steal, kill and destroy; Jesus came that they might have life.
days.codeLine: The thief takes. The Shepherd overflows.

days.title: Walk in Newness of Life

scripture.text: Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life. Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.

days.hook: A muddy, torn shirt goes into a box; the box is taped shut and labelled OLD. The child puts on a clean new shirt. Then the presenter starts peeling the tape. Child: "No! That's buried!"

points.head: The old you was buried.
points.body: "We are buried with him… into death." In Christ, the old life of lying, anger and sin went into the grave with Jesus. You don't dig up what God has buried.

points.head: New life is a walk, not a jump.
points.body: "Even so we also should walk in newness of life." New life shows up in daily steps: a new way of speaking at home, of treating classmates, of using your phone. One new step a day.

points.head: Leave the grave clothes behind.
points.body: Lazarus came out of the tomb still wrapped, and Jesus said, "Loose him." Old habits are grave clothes — they belong to the dead you, not the living you. "Old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new."

mirrors.ot: Exodus 14 (Israel walked out of Egypt through the sea and didn't go back)

days.challenge: Bury one old habit — write it down and tear it up.
days.declaration: Old things are passed away. I walk in newness of life.
days.centralTruth: The old you was buried.

days.title: The Light of Life

scripture.text: Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.

days.hook: A dark path marked with tape on the floor. A torch lights only the next step. The child takes it; the light moves one step on. "I can't see the end. I can see the next step."

points.head: Following Jesus means you never walk in darkness.
points.body: Jesus doesn't promise a life without problems. He promises you will not walk in darkness: you won't be lost, confused about who you are, or without direction.

points.head: He lights the next step.
points.body: "Thy word is a lamp unto my feet" (Psalm 119:105). A lamp shows the next step, not the whole road. You may not know your whole future, but you can always know your next right step — so take it.

points.head: Those who follow the Light become light.
points.body: Jesus promises "the light of life" — light you carry with you. He also said, "Ye are the light of the world" (Matthew 5:14). The closer you follow Him, the brighter you shine for others.

mirrors.ot: Exodus 13:21 (the pillar of fire by night)

days.hook: Hold up a branch snapped off a tree beside one still attached. Living His way is not about straining harder; it is staying joined. A branch doesn't try to make fruit — it abides, and the fruit comes.

days.title: Lord, If Thou Hadst Been Here

scripture.text: Therefore his sisters sent unto him, saying, Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick. When Jesus heard that, he said, This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God might be glorified thereby. Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus. When he had heard therefore that he was sick, he abode two days still in the same place where he was. … Then said Martha unto Jesus, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.

days.hook: A child waits at the school gate, checking a watch. Everyone else has been picked up. Then: car headlights, and Mummy's voice — "I'm here." Presenter: "Martha said 'if.' Jesus was about to say 'I AM.'"

points.head: Jesus loved them — and still waited.
points.body: Verse 5 says He loved Martha, Mary and Lazarus; verse 6 says He stayed where He was two more days. The delay was not because He didn't care. Love and waiting can sit side by side. Delay is not denial.

points.head: Both sisters said "if."
points.body: "Lord, if thou hadst been here…" "If" lives in the past, in what could have been. Many of us live there too: if Daddy had a job, if we had money, if that hadn't happened.

points.head: Jesus answers "if" with "I AM."
points.body: From the start He said, "This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God." He was on His way to show them something bigger than a healing. When Jesus arrives, "if" turns into "I AM."

mirrors.ot: Habakkuk 2:3 ("though it tarry, wait for it")

days.centralTruth: Delay is not denial.
days.codeLine: Jesus is never late — He's on His way.

days.title: I AM the Resurrection and the Life

scripture.text: Jesus saith unto her, Thy brother shall rise again. Martha saith unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day. Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this? She saith unto him, Yea, Lord: I believe that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, which should come into the world.

days.hook: The presenter holds a calendar with a sticky note: SOMEDAY. Rips it off, and writes on a new one: TODAY. "Martha said 'one day.' Jesus said, 'I am' — right now."

points.head: Martha believed in "someday."
points.body: She believed in resurrection "at the last day." That was true, but far away. Many people believe God can do great things someday, somewhere, for someone else.

points.head: Jesus said "I am" — now.
points.body: He didn't say, "I will do a resurrection." He said, "I am the resurrection." Resurrection is not a date on a calendar; it is a Person standing in front of her. Wherever Jesus is, resurrection power is present today.

points.head: "Believest thou this?"
points.body: The same question comes to every listener. Martha answered, "Yea, Lord: I believe," before the stone moved and before Lazarus walked out. Our answer to that question changes everything.

mirrors.ot: Exodus 3:14 ("I AM THAT I AM")

days.codeLine: Resurrection isn't a day. It's a Person.

days.title: Jesus Wept

scripture.text: Then when Mary was come where Jesus was, and saw him, she fell down at his feet, saying unto him, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died. When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews also weeping which came with her, he groaned in the spirit, and was troubled, And said, Where have ye laid him? They said unto him, Lord, come and see. Jesus wept. Then said the Jews, Behold how he loved him!

days.hook: A child sits alone, sad. The presenter sits down beside them and says nothing — a full five seconds of silence on camera. Then: "Sometimes the first thing love does is stay."

points.head: The Life feels your pain.
points.body: Jesus "groaned in the spirit, and was troubled." He didn't stand at a distance giving instructions; He stepped into their grief. We have a High Priest who is "touched with the feeling of our infirmities" (Hebrews 4:15).

points.head: Tears come before triumph.
points.body: Jesus knew that in a few minutes He would raise Lazarus — and He still wept. Tears do not mean your faith is weak. The Life cries with you before He calls you out.

points.head: People who carry His life carry His compassion.
points.body: The crowd said, "Behold how he loved him!" When we carry His life, people should see how we love: sitting with the sad and weeping with those who weep (Romans 12:15).

mirrors.ot: Psalm 56:8 (He keeps our tears)

days.title: Take Away the Stone

scripture.text: Jesus said, Take ye away the stone. Martha, the sister of him that was dead, saith unto him, Lord, by this time he stinketh: for he hath been dead four days. Jesus saith unto her, Said I not unto thee, that, if thou wouldest believe, thou shouldest see the glory of God? Then they took away the stone from the place where the dead was laid. … And when he thus had spoken, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth. And he that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with graveclothes: and his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus saith unto them, Loose him, and let him go.

days.hook: A big cardboard "stone" blocks a doorway. Three children roll it away on cue. A voice calls a child's name from off-screen; a child wrapped in loose cloth walks out, and the others unwrap them.

points.head: Our part: roll away the stone.
points.body: "Take ye away the stone." Jesus could have moved it with a word, but He gave the people a part to play. Martha objected — "he stinketh." Obeying sometimes means opening up something that smells: confessing a wrong, forgiving someone, facing what we have hidden.

points.head: His part: He calls the dead by name.
points.body: "Lazarus, come forth." Only Jesus can raise the dead, and He calls by name. He did not shout at the whole graveyard; He called one man. He knows your name too.

points.head: Our part again: untie the living.
points.body: Lazarus came out still bound, and Jesus told the people, "Loose him, and let him go." People who have just found new life need friends to help free them from old habits, shame and fear.

mirrors.ot: 2 Kings 4:32–35 (Elisha and the Shunammite's son)

days.title: Can These Bones Live?

scripture.text: And he said unto me, Son of man, can these bones live? And I answered, O Lord GOD, thou knowest. Again he said unto me, Prophesy upon these bones, and say unto them, O ye dry bones, hear the word of the LORD. Thus saith the Lord GOD unto these bones; Behold, I will cause breath to enter into you, and ye shall live: … So I prophesied as I was commanded: and as I prophesied, there was a noise, and behold a shaking, and the bones came together, bone to his bone. … So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.

days.hook: Dry sticks laid on the floor in the shape of a skeleton. The presenter kneels — and instead of praying over them, speaks to them: "Sticks, hear the word of the Lord." The children laugh. Then the presenter turns to camera: "That's exactly what God told Ezekiel to do."

points.head: God asks about something completely dead.
points.body: The bones were "very many" and "very dry" (37:2). "Can these bones live?" Ezekiel answered honestly: "O Lord GOD, thou knowest." Some situations look just as dead — a broken family, a failing school, a struggling nation.

points.head: Speak to them, not only about them.
points.body: God said, "Prophesy upon these bones." Ezekiel did not only pray about the bones; he spoke God's word to them. Declaring life means speaking God's word straight into the dead situation.

points.head: When he spoke, life came.
points.body: First a noise, then a shaking, then bones coming together — and finally breath and "an exceeding great army." God works through declared words; He "calleth those things which be not as though they were" (Romans 4:17). In His name, we do the same.

mirrors.ot: Ezekiel 37:10

days.title: Everything Shall Live Where the River Goes

scripture.text: And it shall come to pass, that every thing that liveth, which moveth, whithersoever the rivers shall come, shall live: and there shall be a very great multitude of fish, because these waters shall come thither: for they shall be healed; and every thing shall live whither the river cometh. He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. When Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall ye also appear with him in glory. I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.

days.hook: The blue river fabric that has risen on the board all month is pulled free. Children carry it across the floor, out of the studio door and into the street. The camera follows. “The river was never meant to stay on the board.”
days.story: Everything lives where the river goes — and the river flows through you.

points.head: Christ is your life, not a part of it.
points.body: Paul says "Christ, who is our life," not "Christ, who is part of our life." He is not a Sunday slot or a hobby. "I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me." School, family and dreams all flow from Him.

points.head: The river flows out of you.
points.body: "Out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water." Life given to you is meant to flow through you. The Dead Sea takes water in but has no outlet, so it stays dead; in Ezekiel's vision, the river flows into it and heals it (47:8). Life you keep goes stale; life you give away multiplies.

points.head: Wherever the river goes, things live.
points.body: "Every thing shall live whither the river cometh." That means your home, your class, your street and Nigeria. Kids Inspiring Nation means children carrying Life into the nation, one person at a time.

days.centralTruth: Christ is your life, not a part of it.
days.codeLine: Everything lives where the river goes — and the river flows through you.
